_meta.description: Master metadata file for the Dateflation Calculator. Contains currency configuration, data quality ratings, UI transparency messaging, cultural context notes, key statistics, and a complete sources index. This is the single source of truth for the calculator's currency selector and data provenance UI.

currencies.name: US Dollar
currencies.dataQualityMessage: Based on the BMO Real Financial Progress Index (Ipsos, n=2,500 US adults annually, 2025–2026) corroborated by LendingTree, NerdWallet, and Global Dating Insights surveys. CPI trend uses the BLS 'Food Away From Home' sub-index — the most accurate proxy for dining-out inflation in the US.
currencies.culturalContext: The US pioneered the concept of 'dateflation' — the term was popularised by US media in 2023–2024 as food-away-from-home prices spiked post-pandemic. Americans go on fewer dates year-over-year (14 in 2025, 12 in 2026) but spend more per date. Gen Z outspends older generations on dates, likely driven by experience-oriented preferences and social media pressure. 47% of singles say dating is not financially worth it (BMO 2026).
mediaHighlights: BMO 2026: 'Date-flation Hits Hard: Average Date Spend Nears $200'
CNBC April 2026: 'Why some young Americans are dating less in 2026'
NerdWallet 2024: dating costs driving Gen Z to modify date habits

currencies.name: British Pound
currencies.dataQualityMessage: Based on the Velloy Dating Index 2024 (n=4,000 UK adults: 2,000 singles + 2,000 couples) and the Barclays 2025 Gen Z cost-of-dating report. CPI trend uses the ONS CPIH 'Restaurants & Cafes' sub-index (series L557, 2015=100) — a decade-spanning official dataset directly relevant to dating costs.
currencies.culturalContext: UK daters have faced significant cost-of-living pressures that have directly impacted dating behaviour. Barclays 2025 data highlights Gen Z UK daters increasingly opting for lower-cost date formats (drinks only, coffee) over full restaurant dinners. The ONS restaurant CPI rose 35% between 2019 and 2025 — roughly double the pre-pandemic rate. London dates cost approximately 20–30% more than the national average.
mediaHighlights: Velloy Dating Index 2024: UK dating costs £90–£140 per date
The Guardian: Gen Z changing date formats due to cost pressures

currencies.name: Canadian Dollar
currencies.dataQualityMessage: Direct survey data available for 2025 (CAD $173) and 2026 (CAD $174) from the BMO Real Financial Progress Index Canada edition (Ipsos, n=2,500 Canadian adults). Years prior to 2025 are estimated by applying Statistics Canada's 'Food Purchased from Restaurants' CPI sub-index to the 2025 anchor. The CPI trend data is official and precise; the pre-2025 per-date cost figures are calculated estimates, not direct survey measurements.
currencies.cpiSubIndex: Statistics Canada — Food Purchased from Restaurants
currencies.culturalContext: Canada shows one of the strongest signals of dating cost fatigue among the five currencies. 55% of Canadian singles had zero dates in the past year. 50% say dating is not financially worth it. The cost-of-living crisis — Sal Guatieri, BMO Senior Economist, notes consumer prices are 17% higher than 4 years prior — has hit Canadian dating hard. The CAD $173–174/date figure is notably stable 2025–2026, suggesting Canadians are either cutting back or finding ways to contain costs rather than absorbing ongoing increases.
mediaHighlights: BMO Canada 2025: 'Date-flation is Real — Canadians Spending $173 Per Date'
BMO Canada 2026: 'Half of Single Canadians Do Not Believe Dating is Financially Worth It'
Canadian Press coverage of BMO dating cost surveys

currencies.name: Australian Dollar
currencies.dataQualityMessage: One confirmed direct survey data point: AUD $154.16 for a first date (July 2022, Yahoo Finance Australia survey). All other years are estimated by applying the ABS 'Meals Out and Take Away Foods' CPI sub-index to this anchor. The CPI trend is official; the per-date cost baseline is derived from a single survey source with an undisclosed sample size. First-date costs may be slightly higher than average ongoing-date costs.
currencies.cpiSubIndex: ABS CPI — Meals Out and Take Away Foods (Weighted Average of 8 Capital Cities)

keyStats.restaurantInflationVsGeneralInflation: Restaurant prices rose ~39% vs general CPI ~25% since 2017
keyStats.trendNote: Sydney Morning Herald (July 2023) explicitly reported Australians shifting from restaurant dates to drinks-only dates due to cost-of-living pressures

currencies.culturalContext: Australia's cost-of-living crisis has had a documented impact on dating behaviour. The ABS 'Meals Out' sub-index rose 38.7% between 2017 and 2025 — one of the steeper increases in this dataset. Sydney Morning Herald reporting from 2023 directly noted daters moving to cheaper date formats. Sydney and Melbourne see prices 15–25% above national averages, making city dating particularly expensive.
mediaHighlights: Yahoo Finance Australia July 2022: 'Aussies spending $150 on a first date'
Sydney Morning Herald July 2023: Cost-of-living crisis affecting dating choices
ABS CPI March 2026: Meals out continues to outpace general inflation

currencies.name: Japanese Yen
currencies.dataQualityMessage: Multiple independent Japanese surveys provide per-date cost data: trami.jp 2023 (combined date cost ¥12,491), kanetohonne.jp 2024 (by age group), laskoi.jp 2025 (spending guidelines by gender). The Statistics Bureau of Japan publishes an annual 'Eating Out' (gaishoku, 外食) CPI sub-index with data going back to 2010. Important: Japanese dating data represents per-person or gender-split costs — men traditionally pay more. All figures clearly note whether they are per-person or combined.
currencies.cpiSubIndex: Statistics Bureau of Japan CPI — Eating Out (外食, Gaishoku), Base 2020=100
currencies.cpiSource: Statistics Bureau of Japan, Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications

keyStats.japanDatingNorm: Men pay significantly more than women — this is a persistent cultural norm across age groups, though it is shifting gradually with younger generations
keyStats.matchingAppDominant: Pairs (Match Group) — men pay, women use free

currencies.culturalContext: Japan's dating economy is culturally distinctive in several important ways. Men traditionally bear the majority of dating costs — this is reflected in Japanese dating surveys, where per-person costs are almost always broken down by gender. Japan's eating-out CPI was unusually stable from 2011–2021 (reflecting deflationary pressures), then accelerated sharply post-2021 as the yen weakened and import costs rose. By 2025 the eating-out index was 19.2% above its 2020 base. Dating apps in Japan operate on a gender-asymmetric model (men pay for messaging; women message free) — Pairs being the dominant example. The concept of 'konkatsu' (marriage-hunting activities) adds an additional formal and costly dating layer specific to Japan.
mediaHighlights: trami.jp 2023: Japanese dating cost survey (per-gender breakdown)
kanetohonne.jp 2024: Dating costs by age group in Japan
laskoi.jp 2025: Cost guidelines for dating in Japan
Josei Jishin magazine: Regular coverage of Japanese dating economics

globalKeyFindings.description: Cross-currency headline statistics for the Dateflation Calculator summary section.

findings.finding: US dating costs rose 12.5% from 2025 to 2026 — far outpacing general inflation of ~3%.
55% of single Canadians went on zero dates in the past 12 months.
findings.source: BMO Real Financial Progress Index Canada 2025

findings.finding: UK restaurant prices rose 50% between 2015 and 2025 (ONS CPIH L557).
Australian meals-out prices rose 38.7% between 2017 and 2025, outpacing general CPI.
findings.source: ABS CPI — Meals Out and Take Away Foods

findings.finding: Japan's eating-out CPI rose 19.2% between 2020 and 2025, after nearly a decade of near-zero change.
findings.source: Statistics Bureau of Japan CPI — Eating Out (Gaishoku)

findings.finding: 47% of American singles say dating is not financially worth it (2026).
50% of single Canadians say dating is not financially worth it (2026).
findings.source: BMO Real Financial Progress Index Canada 2026

findings.finding: Hinge Preferred (USD) rose from $12.99/month in 2019 to $34.99 in 2026 — a 169% increase in 7 years.
findings.source: Match Group filings, Business of Apps

findings.finding: The average American who dates spends $2,323/year on dates in 2026, up from $2,279 in 2025.
Japanese men spend ¥7,000–12,000 per date vs ¥3,000–5,000 for women — a 2–3x gap driven by cultural payment norms.
